title: Some Roles Dustin Hoffman was considered turned down or almost lost or almost got almost didn’t take.

commenti.body: I think this is common with a lot of great actors. They turn down stuff they should’ve taken or maybe roles that just weren’t met for them. Dustin Hoffman, the great actor that he is, is kind of this soft spoken nerdy guy. Can you *really* see him doing well in The Godfather? Some directors are great directors but they are bad salespeople and they can’t convey how great their script is to actors. Steve McQueen turned down Close Encounters because he thought it was a B grade science fiction movie, he wasn’t impressed with the script and just didn’t get it. Eddie Murphy turned down Ghostbusters and said “sounds like some weird shit to me.” Gene Hackman turned down Silence of the Lambs because of the violence.
[removed]

My favourite piece of Hoffman trivia:

In 1970 the Weather Underground, a militant anti-vietnam-war student-led organisation, accidentally blew up the Manhattan townhouse they were operating from whilst making bombs in the basement. This destroyed their house as well as a significant portion of the neighbouring house attached to theirs - which just so happened to belong to [Dustin Hoffman](https://blankobtest.wpenginepowered.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/Dustin-Hoffman-BOmbing.jpeg)!

There were some crazy stories about Scorsese in the 1970s:

>The legend goes that Scorsese stayed up all night drinking, getting drunk with a loaded gun. And his purpose was, in the morning he was going to shoot the executive at Columbia for making him cut his masterpiece. And it turned out to be a vigil all night as Scorsese sat there with a loaded gun in his lap and some of his fellow filmmakers and friends came and talked to him and commiserated with him and tried to talk him out of it. And apparently this lasted all night long. I’ve heard stories that literally all of them grew up that night because they realized how serious Scorsese was at the prospect of what he was going to do.

https://bedfordandbowery.com/2016/06/brian-de-palma-shed-light-on-a-crazy-rumor-about-scorsese-and-taxi-driver/

‘He’s the head of the studio he’s the guy I’m angry at, so I’m gonna get a gun and shoot him.’ 

I can just hear Scorsese saying this. Lolz. I know he was a big cocaine user in those days too. Which I’m sure played in to all of this. I’d love to hear specifically Dustin Hoffman’s thoughts at the time.

Pacino would’ve been better than Hoffman in Marathon Man who I feared tampered with the film to get the good guy ending had they gone with a darker or more realistic ending the film would be considered a masterpiece I’ve read Hoffman refused to shoot the bad guy at the end thinking it would hurt his character and tampered with the film like he desperately tried to change Papillion (he was a diva and clashed with McQueen and was such a baby he complained about his less pay and second billing in the film) I think Pacino would’ve done a much much better job I’m afraid and I am a Hoffman fan.

I can't help loving these 'almost was' lists. 

It's crazy how many times Hoffman was in the running with Pacino. They seem like such radically different personas. Having said that, I can imagine Hoffman in Dog Day Afternoon. But The Godfather? Nnn-no. 

The other roles I can imagine Hoffman making a good job of are the ones that went to Richard Dreyfuss (I'm assuming Hoffman was offered the Dreyfuss role in Jaws). Actors with a similar vibe maybe. 

Roles that, to my mind, could only be Hoffman - Kramer Vs Kramer, All The President's Men, and of course, Tootsie. Even though his performance in the Graduate is iconic, I can actually imagine a number of the other candidates playing Benjamin, especially Charles Gordon. Cliff Gorman in Lenny would have been cool to see.
I actually would like to have seen James Caan in Kramer vs Kramer. Something about his tough-guy exterior being a sensitive parent.
Scorsese was a coke fiend in the 70s
My mistake he actually called him crazy not a psychopath but it’s almost the same thing.

Matt Damon turning down Avatar because Bourne was in post production is my favourite one of them all.

Not only did Damon lose out on $300m but I think Avatar would have been better with him in it. 

Hollywood what ifs are wild
But he was fine in the end, just slightly less rich. It's not like the dude why couldn't okay wolverine because of MI2 shooting going long, giving the time to Jackman..

Marty was on a coke bender for much of the 70s. Nearly died in 1978, spent 10 days in a hospital. DeNiro brought him the Raging Bull script and convinced him to do it. Stayed clean I think after that. 

I wonder if some of his pay jobs in the 80s are a result of having to get studios happy and confident to give him money. "See, I can deliver for you, Color of Money! Let's work together, I'm clean now!"

I have to disagree about Godfather.

If you look at a movie like Straight Time (very underrated) which came around the same time, he plays a hardened, stoic criminal, and he's great in it.

I don't know if he would have been as great as Pacino, but I think he could have pulled it off.
I don’t think he was very good in papillon he felt miscast.
